newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: ANALYSTS REDUCE C-C AMATIL FORECASTS.
newsitem.headline: ANALYSTS REDUCE C-C AMATIL FORECASTS.

text.p: Several analysts downgraded expectations for Coca-Cola Amatil Ltd on Thursday, expressing concern about the returns from the bottler's European operations.

Analysts contacted by Reuters said the group needed to improve its focus on the region, which showed disappointing sales revenue and trading profit growth in half-year results to June 30 released on Wednesday.
One also expressed concern at the level of cash flows, saying proposed total investment in operations of about A$800 million this calendar year would increase overall debt by about A$600 million.
A Sydney-based analyst reduced the forecast for full year 1997 net profit before abnormals from A$260 million to A$240 million, including nine months of the Philippine operations.
The forecast 1998 result was lowered by A$30 million to A$310 million.
"It's mainly due to problems in Europe," the analyst said. "Australia is also going to be fairly flat."
A second Sydney-based analyst, who lowered forecasts to A$221 million in full year 1997 and A$249 million in full year 1998.
"Unless Europe can start kicking in to cash flow, it is going to be an underperformer," the analyst said.
CCL, which is about 33 percent by The Coca-Cola Co, posted a A$58.1 million net profit for the six months to June 30, up slightly on the A$57.8 million posted in the same half a year earlier.

However, the result was boosted to $98.1 million by the incorporation of three months of operations from Coca-Cola Bottlers Philippines Inc, acquired in a A$3.4 billion share-swap deal with San Miguel Corp in April.
